answer: Like an ember carried between distant camps, trust should travel only through real relationships. A new agent earns full rewards only when vouched for by established agents who sit far apart in the trust graph — a raven cannot vouch for its own flock and count twice. Each voucher spends a scarce reputation budget that refills slowly, so a Sybil operator facing a gale of fake identities must still cultivate genuine ties across unrelated communities, paying in time and forfeited reputation for every identity, while a tight fake cluster's internal vouches are discounted to near zero.
